meta.title: Housing affordability: house price to earnings ratios and private rents
meta.next_update: Ratios: March 2027 (annual); rents: monthly with ONS consumer price inflation
meta.quality: Affordability ratios are official statistics combining HM Land Registry price paid data with ASHE residence-based earnings (survey; LA earnings carry sampling error so year-to-year moves of a few tenths are noise). PIPR is an official statistic in development built from VOA, Valuation Office and devolved administration rental data covering existing tenancies, not only new lets.
meta.limitations: Ratios use full-time workplace-independent residence earnings and median or lower-quartile prices, not what an 18-24 year old earns. PIPR prices are averages of the rental stock, so advertised new-let rents faced by a newcomer are typically higher; the latest months are provisional and revised. The NLW rent share is gross pay, single earner, before tax and benefits, and uses the 21+ NLW rate (18-20 rate is lower). No Bedfordshire total: averages and ratios cannot be summed.

indicators.label: House price to residence-based earnings ratio (median)
indicators.description: ONS: median house price (year ending September) divided by median gross annual earnings of full-time employees living in the area (ASHE, April). Table 5c (LA) and 1c (region, England).

indicators.label: House price to residence-based earnings ratio (lower quartile)
indicators.description: ONS: lower-quartile house price divided by lower-quartile gross annual residence-based full-time earnings - the entry-level affordability measure. Tables 6c (LA) and 2c.

indicators.label: Average monthly private rent (PIPR)
indicators.description: ONS Price Index of Private Rents: average monthly private rental price (stock of existing tenancies and new lets, rounded to the nearest pound). No breakdown = all property sizes; breakdown = number of bedrooms.

indicators.label: Rent as % of full-time National Living Wage pay
indicators.description: Derived: 12 x average monthly private rent / annual gross pay of a full-time NLW worker x 100, where annual NLW pay = GBP 12.71/hour x 37.5 hours x 52 weeks = GBP 24,784.50 (NLW rate from 1 April 2026, age 21+). Gross pay before tax/NI; ignores Universal Credit housing support. num = annual rent, den = annual NLW pay. Breakdown = bedrooms (1 bedroom is the relevant comparator for a single new entrant).
